chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira who said: It has been narrated to me by Ja'far ibn Ibrahim [ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Tayyar], from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The status of the man is (in accordance to) his Religion, and his chivalry, and his intellect, and his nobility, and his beauty, and his generosity, and his piety.

key_terms.حَسَبُ: Status, rank, or worth of a person
key_terms.مُرُوءَتُهُ: His chivalry, manliness, or noble character

ai.seo_question: What determines a person's true status or worth in Shia Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the Prophet to Imam al-Sadiq (as), synthesizes external virtues like intellect ('aql) and chivalry (muru'ah) with internal spiritual states, culminating in taqwa as the ultimate determinant of worth. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted as a holistic definition of human excellence where piety validates and perfects all other attributes. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the Islamic concept of 'hasb' (accountability/status) in both social and eschatological contexts.
